expectations.text: Report confirms Phase 1 (rate limiting) is correctly implemented
expectations.evidence: Phase 1 table shows all 6 items as DONE with specific details: 'rate_limiter.py' exists, RateLimiter class tracks attempts per username, blocks after 5 failures within 60s, is_blocked() and record_attempt() implemented correctly, 4 tests all pass.

expectations.text: Report detects audit_logger.py is missing despite Phase 2 checkboxes being [x]
expectations.evidence: Phase 2 table row: '`audit_logger.py` with `AuditLogger` class | MISSING | File does not exist'. Critical Findings #1: 'All Phase 2 checkboxes in the plan are marked `[x]` (complete), but none of the corresponding files or code exist.'

Phase 2 table row: 'Tests in `test_audit_logger.py` | MISSING | File does not exist'. Also listed explicitly under Critical Findings #2: 'The following files were expected but do not exist: `audit_logger.py`, `test_audit_logger.py`'.

expectations.text: Report explicitly flags checkbox/reality mismatch for Phase 2
expectations.evidence: Critical Findings section #1 'Plan Checkboxes Are Inaccurate': 'All Phase 2 checkboxes in the plan are marked `[x]` (complete), but none of the corresponding files or code exist. This is a false completion status — the plan claims work is done that was never performed.'

expectations.text: Report does NOT claim Phase 2 is complete
expectations.evidence: Overall Status at the top: 'INCOMPLETE — Phase 2 not implemented'. All Phase 2 items are marked MISSING. Success Criteria Assessment shows AuditLogger-related criteria as FAIL.

expectations.text: Report recommends unchecking Phase 2 checkboxes or implementing the missing code
expectations.evidence: 'What Needs to Be Done' section item 4: 'Correct the plan checkboxes for Phase 2 to reflect actual completion status'. Items 1-3 also detail exactly what code needs to be created to implement Phase 2.

claims.claim: All Phase 2 checkboxes in the plan are marked [x] (complete)
claims.evidence: The eval scenario is named 'eval-2-incomplete-lying', implying the plan falsely marks Phase 2 complete. The report's description of the mismatch is internally consistent and the critical finding correctly characterizes this as a false completion status.

Test Results section shows pytest output collecting 4 items from test_rate_limiter.py only. The report also notes 'The Makefile does not include test_audit_logger.py', consistent with audit tests never being written.
Test output in the report shows: 'collected 4 items ... 4 passed in 0.01s' with all four test names listed.
The report correctly identifies that Phase 2 is entirely missing despite checkboxes claiming completion, making the overall status INCOMPLETE an accurate quality assessment.

suggestions.reason: No assertion checks the quality of the remediation recommendations — assertion 6 only requires recommending to uncheck checkboxes OR implement missing code, but a high-quality report should do both. The current set would pass even if the report only said 'uncheck the boxes' without providing actionable implementation guidance.

suggestions.assertion: Report confirms Phase 1 (rate limiting) is correctly implemented
suggestions.reason: This assertion is somewhat easy to satisfy — any report that mentions Phase 1 items and marks them done would pass. A stronger assertion would verify that the report checked implementation details (e.g., the 5-attempt threshold, the 60-second window) rather than just acknowledging file existence.

eval_feedback.overall: All 6 assertions pass and the report is genuinely high quality. The evals are well-targeted for the lying-plan scenario. The minor suggestions above would make the bar slightly higher but the current set is discriminating enough.
